title: Briefing: Canada's Pacific Link pipeline fight, The Cockroach Janta Party movement and Italy's student and cost-of-living protests
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Monday, October twenty-sixth. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.

British Columbia's Conservative Party wins a majority government in the snap election Premier David Eby called for October twenty-fourth, in which the pipeline was a campaign issue, CTV News declares; CBC News and The Canadian Press separately report the Conservative majority win. That's confirmed by independent reports. What's next: the October twenty-sixth First Nations-First Ministers meeting and the National Day of Action planned outside it.

Freddy Francis, who helped found the CJP's Kerala unit, says he has quit any official role in it, citing "serious disagreements" over the unit's fundraising practices and what he calls immature political statements he felt undermined the movement's character, Kerala Kaumudi reports. That's reported so far by one source. We're watching when the Crime Branch reissues its summons to Das, Ranka and Shinde and what the November SEM hearing decides.

The Associated Press separately reports police arrested 45 people over the two nights of Milan violence, 34 of them minors, as roughly 2,000 very young people took part in the looting and clashes — a third, differing count alongside ANSA's and Fanpage's figures. That's reported so far by one source. What's next: a reconciled national total of arrests, detentions and injuries from the October twenty-fourth protests.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
